# TW Framework — Complete Reference for AI Coding Assistants
# Source: https://github.com/ffakraj-ui/twlang
# Version: v0.8.36 (2026-08-10)
# Rule: If README and source code disagree, trust the source code and tests.

---

## 1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

TW Framework (package: `tw-framework` on PyPI) is a Python-based full-stack web framework with Virtual DOM, App Router, Zero-JS static sites, NPM package manager, React compatibility, and esbuild bundling.

- **Language**: Custom DSL (`.tw` pages/components/layouts, `.tss` stylesheets, `.twm` API routes)
- **Runtime**: Python (compiler + dev server + CLI). API routes (`.twm`) run on Node.js.
- **Package manager**: `pip install tw-framework` (Python). NPM packages via `tw install` command.
- **File extensions**: `.tw` (pages/components/layouts), `.tss` (stylesheets), `.twm` (API routes/lib modules)
- **Project root marker**: `tw.config` file
- **Source folder**: `[home]/` (literal brackets — App Router root)

### 1.1 Installation
```bash
pip install tw-framework
# or for development
pip install -e .
```

### 1.2 Quick Start
```bash
pip install tw-framework
tw create my-site
cd my-site
tw build
```

### 1.3 Project Structure (App Router)
```
my-project/
  tw.config                  # Required. Simple key-value config.
  package.json               # Optional. For npm dependencies (tw install).
  [home]/                    # App Router root (literal brackets)
    layout.tw                # Root layout
    page.tw                  # Home page (route: /)
    about/
      page.tw                # Route: /about
    blog/
      page.tw                # Route: /blog
      [slug]/
        page.tw              # Dynamic route: /blog/:slug
      (dashboard)/           # Route group (doesn't appear in URL)
      layout.tw
      stats/
        page.tw              # Route: /stats
    api/
      route.twm              # API route: /api
      health/
        route.twm            # API route: /api/health
    not-found.tw             # 404 page
    error.tw                # Error boundary
    lib/                     # Lib modules (.twm files for shared logic)
      data.twm
      utils.twm
```

---

## 2. PAGE SYNTAX (`page { }` block)

Every `.tw` page file MUST start with a `page { }` block.

### 2.1 Valid Keys Inside `page { }`

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|-----|------|----------|-------------|
| `title` | string | Yes | Page title. Used in `<title>` tag. |
| `render` | string | No | `static`, `server`, `edge`, `interactive`, `dynamic`. Default: `static`. |
| `layout` | string | No | Layout name (filename without `.tw`). |
| `revalidate` | number | No | ISR — seconds before background regeneration. |
| `responsive` | boolean | No | Enable responsive meta tags. |

### 2.2 Example
```tw
page {
    title "About"
    render static
}

body {
    h1 "About Us"
    p "We build amazing things."
}
```

### 2.3 Render Modes
- `static` — Zero-JS static HTML (default)
- `interactive` — Enables VDOM runtime + React integration
- `server` — Server-side rendering
- `edge` — Edge rendering
- `dynamic` — Dynamic page with `generateStaticParams`

**CRITICAL**: The `page { }` block appears ONLY ONCE at the top of the file.

---

## 3. BODY SYNTAX

The `body { }` block (or `BODY { }`) contains the visual structure.

### 3.1 Tag Syntax Rules

**Pattern 1: Tag with text content**
```tw
h1 "Welcome to TW Framework"
```

**Pattern 2: Tag with attributes only**
```tw
section {
    id "home"
    class "home-hero"
}
```

**Pattern 3: Tag with text AND attributes**
```tw
a "Search Now" {
    href "/#search"
    class "btn btn-primary"
}
```

**Pattern 4: Tag with nested children**
```tw
div {
    class "container"
    h1 "Title"
    p { text "Description paragraph." }
}
```

**Pattern 5: Using `text` pseudo-attribute**
```tw
p {
    class "card-copy"
    text "Some text content."
}
```

### 3.2 Supported HTML Tags
- Structural: `div`, `span`, `section`, `article`, `main`, `header`, `footer`, `nav`, `aside`
- Text: `h1`-`h6`, `p`, `strong`, `em`, `small`, `blockquote`, `pre`, `code`
- Lists: `ul`, `ol`, `li`
- Links/media: `a`, `img`, `video`, `audio`, `source`
- Forms: `form`, `input`, `textarea`, `button`, `label`, `select`, `option`
- Table: `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`
- Meta: `head`, `meta`, `title`, `link`, `script`, `style`

### 3.3 Attribute Syntax
Attributes are space-separated key-value pairs inside `{ }`. NO equals signs. NO colons (except for reactive directives like `on:click`, `bind:value`).

```tw
button {
    type "button"
    class "theme-toggle"
    on:click "__twToggleTheme"
    text "Toggle"
}
```

---

## 4. NPM PACKAGE MANAGER (v0.8.1+)

TW Framework has a built-in NPM package manager — just like Next.js. Install, remove, and list npm packages directly from the TW CLI.

### 4.1 Commands
```bash
tw install react react-dom        # Install packages
tw install chart.js@4.0.0         # Install specific version
tw install --save-dev jest         # Save as devDependency
tw install --exact axios@1.6.0    # Save exact version (no ^)
tw install                         # Install all from package.json
tw add lodash                      # Alias for install
tw remove react                    # Remove a package
tw rm react                        # Alias for remove
tw list                            # List installed packages
tw list --detailed                 # Show installed versions from node_modules
tw ls                              # Alias for list
```

### 4.2 Auto-Detection
TW auto-detects the package manager from lockfiles:
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` → pnpm
- `yarn.lock` → yarn
- `bun.lockb` → bun
- `package-lock.json` → npm

### 4.3 tw.config Integration
`tw install` automatically updates `tw.config` `server.external_packages` so the build system knows which npm packages are allowed.

---

## 5. REACT COMPATIBILITY (v0.8.1+)

Use React alongside TW's native VDOM for islands of interactivity.

### 5.1 Setup
```bash
tw install react react-dom
```

### 5.2 React Component (.twm file)
```javascript
// [home]/lib/react-component.twm
import React, { useState } from "react"

export client function Counter() {
    const [count, setCount] = useState(0)
    return React.createElement("div", { className: "counter" },
        React.createElement("h2", null, "React Counter"),
        React.createElement("p", null, "Count: " + count),
        React.createElement("button", {
            onClick: () => setCount(count + 1)
        }, "Increment")
    )
}
```

### 5.3 React Page (.tw file)
```tw
import { Counter } from "@/lib/react-component"

page {
    title "React Demo"
    render interactive
}

body {
    div { id "react-root" }
    script { on:load "__tw.react.mount('Counter', 'react-root')" }
}
```

### 5.4 How It Works
- `ReactCompat` class in `tw_framework/react_compat.py` detects React usage
- `_inject_react_integration()` in `compiler.py` injects React bootstrap + loader scripts during build
- React bootstrap JS defines `__tw.react` API (mount/unmount/register)
- Loader script uses installed React version (not hardcoded) for CDN, or points to `/js/react-bundle.js` for node_modules bundling
- Config option: `react_cdn` (default: true) — set to `false` to bundle React from node_modules

---

## 6. ESBUILD INTEGRATION (v0.8.1+)

Complex npm packages (like `dayjs`, `chart.js`) are bundled for the browser using esbuild.

### 6.1 How It Works
- `tw_framework/esbuild_integration.py` — detects esbuild availability and bundles packages
- `tw_framework/client_bundler.py` — tries esbuild first, falls back to IIFE wrapper when esbuild is not installed
- esbuild invoked via `npx esbuild` or local install
- `process.env.NODE_ENV` set to `"production"` during bundling

### 6.2 Fallback
When esbuild is not available, a warning is generated: "esbuild is not installed — using fallback IIFE bundler. Complex npm packages may not bundle correctly. Install with: tw install --save-dev esbuild"

---

## 7. LIB SYSTEM

### 7.1 Import Syntax
```tw
import { getApps, getApp } from "@/lib/data"
import formatPrice from "@/lib/utils"

page {
    title "Apps"
    render static
}

let apps = getApps()

body {
    each apps as app {
        div { class "card"
            h1 "{app.name}"
            p "Price: {formatPrice(app.price)}"
        }
    }
}
```

### 7.2 .twm Module Files
```javascript
// Server-side (build-time execution)
export async function getApps() {
    const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/apps");
    return res.json();
}

// Client-side (shipped to browser)
export client function formatPrice(n) {
    return "₹" + n.toFixed(2);
}

// Type annotations (stripped before execution)
export function getApp(slug: string): Promise<App> {
    return getApps().find(a => a.slug === slug);
}
```

### 7.3 NPM Dependencies in .twm
```twm
import dayjs from "dayjs"

export function formatDate(date) {
    return dayjs(date).format("YYYY-MM-DD");
}
```
NPM packages from `node_modules` are properly resolved via `createRequire` in the lib executor bridge script.

---

## 8. VIRTUAL DOM (v0.8.0+)

VDOM is auto-detected. If a page uses `state`, events, or bindings, the VDOM runtime is injected automatically (~3KB, no React dependency).

```tw
page {
    title "Counter"
    render interactive
}

state {
    count 0
    items []
}

body {
    button { on:click "count++" text "Increment" }
    p { tw-text "count" text "" }
    input { bind:value "name" }
    div { show:visible "count > 5" text "Count is high!" }
}
```

Static pages remain Zero-JS — no runtime, no overhead.

---

## 9. REACTIVE BINDINGS

### 9.1 State Declaration
```tw
state {
    count 0
    name "hello"
    items []
    visible true
}
```

### 9.2 Two-way Binding (`bind:value`)
```tw
input {
    type "text"
    bind:value "name"
    placeholder "Enter your name"
}
```

### 9.3 Event Handlers (`on:*`)
```tw
button {
    class "btn"
    on:click "count++"
    text "Increment"
}
```
Available: `on:click`, `on:input`, `on:change`, `on:submit`, `on:keydown`, `on:load`, etc.

### 9.4 Conditional Display (`show:visible`)
```tw
div {
    show:visible "count > 0"
    text "Count is greater than zero"
}
```

### 9.5 Text Binding (`tw-text`)
```tw
span { tw-text "count" }
```

### 9.6 HTML Binding (`tw-html`)
```tw
div { tw-html "htmlContent" }
```

### 9.7 List Rendering (`tw-for`)
```tw
ul {
    tw-for "items"
    li {
        data-tw-for-template ""
        style "display:none"
        text "{item.name}"
    }
}
```

---

## 10. ROUTING (APP ROUTER)

### 10.1 File-Based Routing
```
[home]/
├── layout.tw          ← Root layout
├── page.tw            ← Home page (/)
├── about/
│   └── page.tw        ← /about
├── blog/
│   ├── page.tw        ← /blog
│   └── [slug]/
│       └── page.tw    ← /blog/:slug (dynamic route)
├── (dashboard)/       ← Route group (doesn't appear in URL)
│   ├── layout.tw
│   └── stats/
│       └── page.tw    ← /stats
├── api/
│   └── route.twm      ← API route handler
├── not-found.tw       ← 404 page
└── error.tw           ← Error boundary
```

### 10.2 Route Path Generation (v0.8.36 Fix)
Route paths are generated by three functions, all now consistent:
- `route_path_from_page_info()` in `compiler.py` — used for `__TW_DATA__` JSON and HTML metadata
- `route_from_static_page()` in `framework.py` — used by sitemap.xml and RSS
- `route_from_dynamic_page()` in `framework.py` — used by sitemap.xml for dynamic routes

All three use `url_path` first (from App Router discovery), then fall back to `rel_dir` + `name` with duplicate detection. This fixes the `/about/about` double-nesting bug.

### 10.3 Pretty URLs
When `pretty_urls: true` in `tw.config` (default):
- `/about` → `dist/about/index.html` (NOT `dist/about/about/index.html`)
- `/` → `dist/index.html`
- App Router pages: `rel_dir` already contains the route name, so `page_info["name"]` is NOT appended again

---

## 11. API ROUTES (`.twm` files)

API routes use `.twm` extension and run on Node.js runtime.

### 11.1 File Naming
Every API endpoint file MUST be named `route.twm`.

| File | Route |
|------|-------|
| `[home]/api/route.twm` | `/api` |
| `[home]/api/health/route.twm` | `/api/health` |
| `[home]/api/auth/login/route.twm` | `/api/auth/login` |

### 11.2 Handler Functions
```twm
fn get(request) {
    return { ok: true, message: "Hello from GET" };
}

fn post(request) {
    return { status: 201, json: { ok: true, created: true } };
}

// Generic handler (catches all methods)
fn handler(request) {
    return { json: { method: request.method } };
}

// Async
async fn get(request) {
    const data = await http.get("https://api.example.com/data");
    return { json: data };
}
```

### 11.3 Request Object
- `request.method` — HTTP method string
- `request.path` — normalized URL path
- `request.query` — query parameters object
- `request.body` — parsed body (JSON/form/raw)
- `request.headers` — headers object
- `request.cookies` — cookies object
- `request.env` — server environment variables
- `request.project_root` — absolute path to project root

### 11.4 Response Formats
```twm
// Simple string → 200 text/plain
fn get(request) { return "ok"; }

// Auto JSON → 200 application/json
fn get(request) { return { ok: true }; }

// Explicit response
fn get(request) {
    return {
        status: 201,
        headers: { "X-Test": "1" },
        json: { ok: true }
    };
}
```

### 11.5 Built-in Helpers
- `http.get/post/put/patch/delete(url, options?)` — async HTTP client
- `env.KEY` or `env.get("KEY")` or `env.require("KEY")` — environment variables
- `secrets.KEY` or `secrets.get("KEY")` or `secrets.require("KEY")` — secrets
- `pkg.require("package-name")` — load npm package from node_modules
- `firebase.app()`, `firebase.firestore()`, `firebase.auth()` — Firebase Admin helpers

---

## 12. MIDDLEWARE

Middleware is defined in `middleware.tw` in the project root.

```tw
fn before(request) {
    request.headers["X-Custom-Header"] = "middleware-active"
    return request
}

fn after(response) {
    response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY"
    return response
}
```

Return behavior:
- Return `request` → continue with modified request
- Return `null` → continue with original request
- Return response object → halt and return that response
- Return `"skip"` → skip remaining middleware

---

## 13. SERVER ACTIONS (v0.8.0+)

```tw
action createPost {
    method POST
    handler "createPost"
    require_auth true
}

body {
    button { on:click "__twAction('createPost', { title: 'Hello' })" text "Create" }
}
```

---

## 14. SECURITY MODULE (v0.8.1+)

`tw_framework/security.py` provides:
- CSP (Content Security Policy) nonce generation
- Secure HTTP headers
- Input sanitization
- CSRF protection

---

## 15. TSS STYLESHEET SYNTAX

TSS uses whitespace-sensitive, semicolon-free syntax.

```tss
:root {
    --bg-color #f6f8fc
    --text-color #0f172a
}

body {
    margin 0
    background var(--bg-color)
    color var(--text-color)
    font-family Inter, system-ui, sans-serif
}

.btn:hover {
    transform translateY(-2)
}

@media (max-width:768) {
    .container {
        padding 0 18
    }
}
```

**CRITICAL**: NO colons between property and value. NO semicolons at end of lines.

---

## 16. LAYOUTS

Layouts are `.tw` files. They are NOT wrapped in `page { }`.

```tw
component layout {
    html {
        head {
            title "{children.title}"
        }
        body {
            nav { class "navbar"
                a { href "/" text "Home" }
                a { href "/about" text "About" }
            }
            main { class "container"
                children
            }
            footer "© 2026"
        }
    }
}
```

Layout placeholders:
- `{title}` — page title
- `{head}` — head block content
- `{styles}` — loaded stylesheets
- `{slot}` — page body content
- `{scripts}` — generated scripts

## 17. CLI COMMANDS

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `tw create <name>` | Create new App Router project |
| `tw build` | Build site to `dist/` |
| `tw build --prod` | Production build (explicit) |
| `tw dev` | Start dev server (default port 3000) |
| `tw dev --port 4000` | Dev server on custom port |
| `tw serve` | Production server |
| `tw install <pkg>` | Install npm package (v0.8.1+) |
| `tw install` | Install all from package.json |
| `tw install --save-dev <pkg>` | Save as devDependency |
| `tw install --exact <pkg>@ver` | Save exact version |
| `tw add <pkg>` | Alias for install |
| `tw remove <pkg>` | Remove npm package |
| `tw rm <pkg>` | Alias for remove |
| `tw list` | List installed packages |
| `tw list --detailed` | Show installed versions |
| `tw ls` | Alias for list |
| `tw info` | Show project info |
| `tw dead` | Find unused files |
| `tw version` | Show version |

---

## 18. DEPLOYMENT

Output is static HTML/CSS/JS in `dist/`. Deploy to any host:
- Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages
- GitHub Pages
- Any static file server

### Vercel
```json
{
    "framework": "tw",
    "buildCommand": "tw build",
    "outputDirectory": "dist",
    "installCommand": "pip install tw-framework"
}
```

### Netlify
```toml
[build]
  command = "tw build --prod"
  publish = "dist"
```

---

## 19. FRAMEWORK MODULES (v0.8.36)

| Module | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `tw_framework/compiler.py` | Main compiler — lexer, parser, HTML renderer, route path generation |
| `tw_framework/framework.py` | Build pipeline, dev server, route discovery, sitemap/RSS generation |
| `tw_framework/cli.py` | CLI commands (create, build, dev, install, remove, list) |
| `tw_framework/npm_manager.py` | NPM package manager — pnpm/yarn/bun auto-detection |
| `tw_framework/react_compat.py` | React compatibility — bootstrap, loader, version detection |
| `tw_framework/client_bundler.py` | Client-side bundler — esbuild + IIFE fallback, topological sort |
| `tw_framework/esbuild_integration.py` | esbuild detection and bundling |
| `tw_framework/security.py` | CSP nonces, secure headers, input sanitization, CSRF |
| `tw_framework/module_boundaries.py` | Server/client module classification |
| `tw_framework/twm_parser.py` | .twm file parser — imports, exports, async/await |
| `tw_framework/lib_executor.py` | .twm module execution — createRequire, env helpers |
| `tw_framework/js_interop.py` | JS interop — import maps, client bundling delegation |
| `tw_framework/reactivity.py` | Reactive bindings — state, events, bind:*, show:*, tw-* |
| `tw_framework/render_html.py` | HTML document builder |
| `tw_framework/tss_parser.py` | TSS stylesheet parser |

---

## 20. COMMON MISTAKES

1. **Writing JSX instead of TW syntax**
   - WRONG: `<div className="app"><h1>Title</h1></div>`
   - CORRECT: `div { class "app" h1 "Title" }`

2. **Using `=` or `:` in variable declarations**
   - WRONG: `let { name = "hello"; count: 0 }`
   - CORRECT: `let { name "hello" count 0 }`

3. **Writing CSS syntax in TSS files**
   - WRONG: `body { margin: 0; color: #333; }`
   - CORRECT: `body { margin 0 color #333 }`

4. **Using `className` instead of `class`**
   - WRONG: `className "btn-primary"`
   - CORRECT: `class "btn-primary"`

5. **Forgetting `route.twm` naming for API files**
   - WRONG: `[home]/api/users.twm`
   - CORRECT: `[home]/api/users/route.twm`

6. **Using bare strings instead of `text` directive**
   - WRONG: `button { on:click "count++" "+" }`
   - CORRECT: `button { on:click "count++" text "+" }`

7. **Nesting `page { }` inside layouts or components**
   - Layouts are plain template files with `{slot}` placeholders

8. **Using `render` key with invalid values**
   - Valid: `static`, `server`, `edge`, `interactive`, `dynamic`
